---
title: External Links
---

## Overview

HTML output can mark links that leave your site, open them in a new
tab, or both:

``` yaml
format:
  html:
    link-external-icon: true
    link-external-newwindow: true
```

| Option                    | Effect on each external link                                                         |
|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `link-external-icon`      | `true` adds the class `external`, which draws a small box-arrow icon after the text. A string names a [Bootstrap icon](https://icons.getbootstrap.com/) to show instead, e.g. `box-arrow-up-right`. |
| `link-external-newwindow` | `true` adds `target="_blank"` and, unless the link already has a `rel`, `rel="noopener"`. |
| `link-external-filter`    | A regular expression. Links whose URL matches it count as internal.                 |

Both switches are off by default. The options apply to every
HTML-based format, including `revealjs`, and work in project config
(`_quarto.yml`) as well as front matter.

## Which links count as external

Quarto decides when it renders the document, from each link's URL:

- Relative links (`about.qmd`, `../img/x.png`, `#section`) are
  internal.
- Only `http:`, `https:` and protocol-relative `//host/…` URLs can be
  external. `mailto:`, `tel:` and other schemes are left alone.
- Links to `localhost`, on any port, are internal.
- A URL that matches `link-external-filter` is internal.
- On a website without `link-external-filter`, the filter defaults to
  `website.site-url`: absolute links into your own site stay
  internal.
- Everything else is external. Without `site-url` or a filter, that
  means every absolute `http(s)` link.

Only links written in the document body are adorned. Links in raw
HTML (`<a href=…>`) and in navigation chrome (navbar, sidebar,
footer) are not.

## Per-link control

Add `.no-external` to a link to leave it alone:

``` markdown
[Our partner site](https://partner.example.com/){.no-external}
```

You can also adorn a single link by hand, with or without the
options. The icon styling is always included:

``` markdown
[example](https://example.com){.external target="_blank"}
```

A `target` or `rel` you write yourself is kept.

## The filter is a Rust regular expression

`link-external-filter` is compiled with Rust's
[`regex` syntax](https://docs.rs/regex/latest/regex/#syntax). That
syntax has no look-around (`(?=…)`, `(?!…)`, `(?<=…)`, `(?<!…)`) and
no backreferences. A pattern that does not compile produces the
warning [`Q-13-14`](../../../errors/navigation/Q-13-14.qmd) and is
ignored. Quote the pattern in single quotes so that YAML passes its
backslashes through unchanged:

``` yaml
format:
  html:
    link-external-icon: true
    link-external-filter: '^https://(www\.)?quarto\.org/'
```

The pattern is matched anywhere in the URL unless you anchor it with
`^`.

## Differences from Quarto 1

- **Rendering time instead of browser time.** Quarto 1 classified
  links with JavaScript in the reader's browser, so with no
  `site-url` or filter it compared links against the page's own
  host. Quarto 2 cannot know where the page will be served, so an
  absolute link to your own host counts as external unless
  `site-url` or `link-external-filter` covers it.
- **Regex dialect.** Quarto 1 used JavaScript regular expressions.
  Patterns with look-around or backreferences need rewriting.
- **Scope.** Quarto 1 adorned every `<a>` on the page, raw HTML
  included. Quarto 2 adorns body links only. Other URL schemes such
  as `tel:` are never external.
- **String icons.** Quarto 1's schema rejected a string
  `link-external-icon`. Quarto 2 accepts one, places the icon after
  the link, and ships the Bootstrap Icons font for that page.
- **Icon styling.** Quarto 1 included the `.external` icon styling
  only when `link-external-icon` was on. Quarto 2 always includes it.
